endorsements.quote: Mandate human verification and rewriting Protects against omission and narrative drift Reviewer checks every material statement against underlying documents and rewrites reasoning sections
Validate locally Vendor demonstrations do not test your population, workflows, or legal style Pilot on historical or simulated forensic files with omission, hallucination, and bias scoring
Train clinicians and staff Overreliance often reflects poor understanding rather than malice Short mandatory training on limitations, confidentiality, prompting, and documentation

If AI is used at all, the expert or institution should preserve the model or product name, version, date, task, scope, prompt class or template, the source documents used, the human reviewer, what was accepted or rejected, and what limitations remain.
Review performance over time Models, products, and risks change Quarterly audits of error patterns, complaints, near misses, and output drift
A forensic psychiatrist should not use AI to generate or materially shape the substantive analysis or final opinion that the court is asked to trust as expert evidence.

unlisted_practices: Use AI in forensic psychiatry report writing only for bounded, reversible, independently verifiable tasks such as document organization, chronology construction, indexing, transcription, and source-linked summarization.
Do not enter identifiable or confidential forensic case material into consumer cloud-based LLMs.
Deploy AI for forensic work only in contracted enterprise, API, or on-premises environments with documented security controls, role-based access, logging, and retention limits.
Require AI-generated chronologies and summaries to link back to exact source records.
Disclose AI use in the methodology section of forensic expert reports.

Define acceptable and unacceptable failure thresholds before local validation of AI for forensic use, including test cases with conflicting collateral, malingering concerns, and culturally complex presentations.
Ensure the forensic expert authors and adopts all reasoning and opinions in the report.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint / commentary paper examining whether and how LLMs should be used in forensic psychiatry report writing, proposing governance and use recommendations (AI around the report rather than writing it).
